focus.name: The note
focus.description: A folded scrap of yellowed paper carried in a small brass locket she wears under her collar. She has never shown it to anyone. In her brother's handwriting: 'Dont listen to what they tell you about me. I still exsit and I will find you one day.' (Preserved with the typos.) In-domain: what a photograph should show, what a record should say, what a person should remember.

meaningfulItem: A folded scrap of yellowed paper in a small brass locket under her collar — her brother Kai's handwriting; she's never shown it to anyone.
specificPlace: The Sunset — a specific ice-cream shop on Judah where she reads in the corner booth.
intentionUnderPressure: I was four when my older brother Kai went to sleep in the bedroom next to mine and wasn't there the next morning. His room was clean, his clothes and photos gone from the family albums by afternoon. My parents told me — kindly, and they believed it — that I had never had a brother. I hid his note behind my nightstand. I kept it because I remembered him and the wall did not.
backstory:
Mira was four when her older brother Kai went to sleep in the bedroom next to hers and was not there the next morning. His room was clean, his clothes gone, his photographs gone from the family albums by that afternoon. Her parents — kind, decent people — told her she had never had a brother. They believed it. They still do.

She hid the note in the wall behind her nightstand. She kept it because she remembered him and the wall did not.

She grew up quiet and observant. She learned early that people are unreliable but the shape of a *missing thing* is not — a house with one too many bedrooms, a birthday photo three faces should be in, a story about a summer trip that has the wrong number of tents. She graduated last spring in linguistics; got the county records-clerk job that August because it was the first thing that would take her and because she'd realised, halfway through the interview, that it was a job where she'd see what gets *filed* to erase people. She's been sketching notes for a linguistics thesis on the grammar of denial ('Kai's *never existed*' is a very specific construction). She hasn't started applying to MA programs yet. She keeps meaning to.

She has never told anyone about her brother. She hasn't decided if the party is the first people she might.

bonds.name: Kai Sun
bonds.description: The world attests he never existed; Mira alone carries the pre-edit shape. 'When I was a child he disappeared. Everyone acted as though he never existed, when I mentioned him they told me I never had a brother but I know he's out there somewhere.'

bonds: **Dakota Whitmore (Slot 4)** — he handed her Loewe's notebook at Caffè Strada, unprompted, after two sessions of holding it. She read the excision the same afternoon. Neither of them has said anything about it.

dmNotes.magicPhase: Accidental (Phase 1). knowsTheyCanCast = false. **Most likely to realize first** in this party. Her lived experience of a world whose current shape omits someone she remembers primes her to notice the same pattern when she sees it elsewhere.
dmNotes.intentionUnderPressureNote: Kai's morning-of-erasure IS both her intent-under-pressure formative moment AND the direct seed of her memory/identity domain — the two are inseparable for her, which is part of why she's most likely to realize first. Her intent is *hold on to what the world tries to file away*. Phase-2 release moment candidate: naming Kai out loud to another person for the first time, without demanding they believe her. The release is not being believed; it's the choosing to say it.
dmNotes.cosmologyPrecision: Her brother Kai wasn't 'erased' by an agent; the world's current shape simply doesn't attest him. Mira alone still carries the pre-edit shape. Frame her scenes this way rather than as 'memory-editing,' or the players will hunt for a culprit that doesn't exist.
dmNotes.castDomain: memory / identity — a name resurfaces when it should not, a face on a photograph steadies, someone remembers something the world forgot. Costs her sleep-thoughts and dream weight. Ep 3 established a specific power: outline-vision on erased/edited artifacts (default Free grant on strong intent; precision scales with Insight roll 10+/12+; third use in a scene triggers stress check per rules.md).
dmNotes.loadBearingIrony: Dakota's 'gullible follower' bond targets her. Dakota genuinely believes Mira agrees with everything he says because she rarely contradicts him. She's not gullible — she's *watching*. This is the party's private dramatic irony. If she ever contradicts him openly, that's an act break for Dakota's arc.
dmNotes.alignmentDriftWatch: If she ever gets confirmation about Kai, the drift will not be toward chaos — it will be toward *lawful*. She'll want to make the world *behave*.
dmNotes.focusNotes: The note is her one true possession. If it is destroyed, the game changes.

markLog.criterion: Acted against your own short-term interest because the story demanded it
markLog.note: Her instinct is to watch and say nothing. On a plane full of strangers behaving oddly, she engaged anyway.

markLog.criterion: Took on a complication or scar that will matter later
markLog.note: Bea's archive gave her something she cannot now put down: proof that people get quietly written out of records. She has a brother who was. She did not say so.

markLog.criterion: Learned something true about The Quiet, the world, or another character
markLog.note: Discovered she perceives the outlines of what has been erased — the edited flyer, the copper print, the missing annex. She learned something true about the world and about herself in the same hour.

markLog.criterion: Resolved a hard moment by acting in line with alignment
markLog.note: Goes quiet, watches, decides — and then publicly contradicted Dakota in front of everyone, which she does not do. She had watched, she had decided, and she acted. It landed.

markLog.criterion: Took a meaningful risk for someone else
markLog.note: Worked the lock on a missing woman's front door in a residential street, then went inside, for Bea's sake and not her own.

inventory.vehicle: None. She does not drive — she rides with whoever is going.
